message.content:
Can you help me draft a power of attorney document tailored to my needs?

Yes — I can help. Below is a clear, reproducible example that answers the question and shows how to draft a simple power of attorney (POA). Read through it to see structure, typical clauses, and how to adapt it to specific needs.

Example: Simple General Power of Attorney (explanatory paragraphs and template)

1) Purpose and parties
- A power of attorney is a legal document where one person (the principal) authorizes another person (the agent or attorney-in-fact) to act on the principal’s behalf.
- Use a POA when you want someone to manage your affairs (financial, property, or personal) if you cannot do so yourself or prefer someone else to act.

2) Choose the type and scope
- General POA: broad powers to handle many affairs (banking, contracts, taxes, real estate).
- Limited (special) POA: powers limited to a particular act or time period (e.g., selling a specific car).
- Durable vs. non-durable: a durable POA remains effective if the principal becomes incapacitated; a non-durable POA ends on incapacity.

3) Key elements to include
- Principal’s full name and address.
- Agent’s full name and address.
- Effective date and whether the POA is durable.
- Specific powers granted (list clearly).
- Any limitations or conditions.
- Signatures, date, and any required witnesses/notary.

4) Example template (fill in bracketed items)
POWER OF ATTORNEY

I, [Principal’s Full Name], residing at [Principal’s Address], hereby appoint [Agent’s Full Name], residing at [Agent’s Address], as my attorney-in-fact to act in my name, place, and stead.

1. Grant of General Authority
I grant my agent full authority to manage and conduct all of my affairs, including but not limited to: banking transactions; handling investments; filing and paying taxes; purchasing, selling, and managing real property; entering into contracts; and handling claims and litigation on my behalf.

2. Special Limitations (if any)
This power of attorney does not authorize the agent to: [list any specific acts the agent may not perform, e.g., make gifts exceeding $____, change beneficiary designations, or dissolve business interests without my written consent].

3. Effective Date and Durability
This power of attorney shall become effective on [effective date] and shall remain in effect until [expiration date] / OR shall be durable and remain in effect notwithstanding my subsequent incapacity.

4. Revocation
I reserve the right to revoke this power of attorney at any time by providing written notice to my agent.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have executed this Power of Attorney on this [day] of [month], [year].

________________________________
[Principal’s Signature]

Witnesses:
1. ______________________________
Name: ___________________________

2. ______________________________
Name: ___________________________

State of _______________________
County of ______________________

Subscribed and sworn before me this ____ day of ____________, 20__.

________________________________
Notary Public
My commission expires: __________

5) How to adapt and use
- For a limited POA, replace the broad “Grant of General Authority” with a specific list of powers and add start/end dates.
- To make it durable, include language such as “This power of attorney shall not be affected by my subsequent incapacity.”
- Check local legal requirements for witness/notary rules and any language required by state law.

6) Example scenario
Suppose you need someone to manage your bank accounts and pay bills while you work abroad for six months. Use a limited POA naming the agent, list only “banking transactions” and “bill payments” as powers, set the effective date and an expiration date six months later, and sign with any required witnesses or notary.

This example demonstrates the meaning implied by “help” (assist in creating the document) by actually providing a draft and clear instructions you can reproduce and adapt.
